title: NSA classified internal network disrupted
summary: A classified NSA network was disrupted. The agency attributed network degradation to scheduled maintenance. An intrusion has not been established.
connection: No validated public technical connection with FAA, Microsoft, Chase, or Optimizely.

title: Optimizely scripts compromised across 178 organizations
summary: Malicious JavaScript appeared in customer website projects. Reported capabilities included credential theft, crypto wallet hijacking, and mobile exploit targeting. Victim impact under investigation.
connection: A compromised shared technology supplier explains the cross-site exposure, but does not establish connection to other infrastructure outages.

title: Chase processing incident affects transactions
summary: Banking transaction disruption affected payments and transfers, reportedly with downstream effects at other banks. Cyber intrusion has not been demonstrated.
connection: Cross-bank processing dependencies can propagate outages; not evidence of one attacker.

title: United Airlines departure system disrupted
summary: A technology problem delayed flight departures. United attributed the problem to a software issue.
connection: Distinct incident from November 13 FAA ground stop.

title: FAA telecommunications failure causes ground stop
summary: Network and communications disruption caused a nationwide ground stop. Published explanations cite equipment and network instability; no verified cyberattack identified.
connection: No matching compromise indicators publicly demonstrated for other incidents.

title: Coordinated phishing campaign exploits Microsoft 365 outage
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a high-volume malicious phishing campaign using fabricated outage/service-health emails and fraudulent prompts to restore held messages. Intent was assessed as credential theft; Microsoft did not confirm successful credential submission or downstream compromise.
confidence: High (observed phishing campaign); no confirmed credential capture
connection: Confirmed opportunistic exploitation of the widely reported Microsoft service outage, not evidence that phishing actors caused that outage.

title: Microsoft 365 enterprise service disruption
summary: November 12–13 global Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online outage disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and related services. A subsequent post-incident report described an older software defect combined with traffic changes and limited server capacity. UK government, NHS, police and Parliament were among affected users.
connection: Direct service dependency links the Microsoft outage with UK government and public-service disruptions. A phishing campaign separately exploited the outage as a lure; it is not evidence the attackers caused the service outage.

title: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts UK government, NHS, police and Parliament
summary: During November 12–13 Microsoft 365 disruption, UK public-sector users experienced failures involving email and other productivity systems. UK Parliament, NHS services and Metropolitan Police operations reported impacts. Emergency and other critical functions remained operational according to the government.
connection: Direct shared dependency on Microsoft 365 with the global outage. Distinct from Gibraltar's earlier confirmed unauthorized cloud access.

title: Maersk confirms breach through legacy logistics platform
summary: Maersk acknowledged unauthorized access involving a legacy platform acquired with LF Logistics; WhiteArmor claimed responsibility and ransom demands, while wider infrastructure disruption was not reported.
confidence: High (confirmed breach); actor identity based on claim
connection: Supply-chain and legacy-system exposure; no publicly proven shared attacker with other November incidents.

title: Gibraltar government confirms unauthorized access to Microsoft cloud environment
summary: Disclosed November 9, with intrusion occurring weeks earlier. Government officials reported unauthorized access to cloud services including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. Microsoft alerted authorities; the UK NCSC assisted investigations. Extent of personal data exposure was under investigation.
connection: Confirmed link to Microsoft's cloud services and incident-response support, NOT evidence that this earlier compromise caused the separate November 12 Microsoft 365 global outage.

title: Ransomware disrupts services at 66 Queens Public Library branches
summary: Queens Public Library confirmed a ransomware attack that interrupted public computers, Wi-Fi, checkouts and digital systems across its branch network; recovery continued into mid-November.
connection: No documented link to the Microsoft, FAA or NSA outages.

title: UK government clarifies October PHP vulnerability service shutdowns
summary: On November 2 the UK government clarified that several public-facing services were taken offline in October as a precaution against critical PHP vulnerabilities. It reported no confirmed government website compromises from the vulnerability. Included as November follow-up to an October event.
confidence: High (official account); initial disruption in October
connection: Separate vulnerability-response event, not a proven intrusion into UK central-government systems.

title: Stolen third-party access key leads to 44-hour cloud intrusion
summary: From November 1–2 an attacker used a stale cloud key previously shared with an AI vendor to traverse approximately 10 cloud accounts, reach stored secrets and Kubernetes infrastructure. Barracuda reported behavior consistent with ARTEX; victim attribution remains unknown.
connection: Confirmed supplier credential dependency. No validated indicator ties this intrusion to the global Microsoft service outage.
